Name: Choi Hung Estate basketball court
Location: 2 Tse Wai Avenue, Ngau Chi Wan (rooftop car park), Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Pastel-coloured 1960s public housing blocks around a rooftop basketball court. Why: Hong Kong's most photographed housing estate and still a working home.

Name: Ping Shek Estate
Location: Near Choi Hung MTR Exit A2, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Curved concrete blocks with a central courtyard for upward symmetry shots. Why: Quieter than Choi Hung, five minutes away.

Name: Monster Building (Montane Mansion, Yick Cheong and Yick Fat)
Location: King's Road, Quarry Bay (Taikoo MTR), Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Interlinked 1980s residential blocks forming a dense facade. Why: Hollywood-famous HK density image.

Name: Mong Kok and Yau Ma Tei neon
Location: Nathan Road, Mong Kok and Yau Ma Tei, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The remaining neon signs, such as the Gam Lai Gung Karaoke signs and Wo Hing Victory Mahjong at 385 Nathan Road. Why: Signs keep coming down under building codes; a few were removed in 2026.

Name: Lugard Road lookout
Location: Lugard Road, The Peak, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A free skyline vantage on the Peak Circle Walk. Why: Same view as Sky Terrace 428 without the fee or the crowds.

Name: Instagram Pier (Western District)
Location: Western District Public Cargo Working Area, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Working cargo pier popular for photos. Why: Marine Department warns of fines for trespassing.

Name: Kennedy Town Promenade and harbour views
Location: New Praya, Kennedy Town, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Steep streets drop straight to the harbour; a nearby playground basketball court frames Catchick Street and the water through a fence. Why: A sunset vantage with fewer visitors than Central.

Name: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade and Avenue of Stars
Location: Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The harbourfront promenade with a head-on view of the Central skyline and the nightly Symphony of Lights at 20:00. Why: The classic skyline shot; less crowded at sunrise.

Name: Braemar Hill lookout
Location: Braemar Hill, North Point, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A hillside lookout reached by a 20-30 minute unmarked walk, recommended for harbour sunset. Why: A local-photographer favourite; haze in winter can hide towers.

Name: Kowloon Peak (Fei Ngo Shan)
Location: Fei Ngo Shan Road, Ma On Shan Country Park, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Late-afternoon viewpoint over Kowloon estates and mountain ranges. Why: Hard hike, big reward.

Name: Graham Street mural and market
Location: Graham Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A bright mural beside a long-running street market. Why: Narrow street; traffic safety issues cited.

Name: Ocean Terminal Deck
Location: Harbour City, Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Waterfront deck where junk boats drift past at sunset. Why: Sunset spot with a dependable harbour view.

Name: West Kowloon Waterfront Promenade
Location: West Kowloon Cultural District, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Open promenade with harbour views, beside M+ and the Palace Museum. Why: An easy skyline shot any hour.

Name: Lee Tung Avenue
Location: Lee Tung Avenue, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Pedestrian street of shops and restaurants on the old Wedding Card Street, which has staged Christmas light and snow displays in past years. Why: A walkable festive stop with heritage tie-ins to Wan Chai's wedding-card printers.

Name: Yau Ma Tei Wholesale Fruit Market
Location: Shek Lung Street, Yau Ma Tei, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: 1913 wholesale fruit market (Grade III historic) whose workers begin around midnight, stacking crates and loading carts under old shopfronts. Why: Time Out cites it among the best street-photography spots; the lit crates and pre-dawn labour suit film and candid work.

Name: Central-Mid-Levels Escalator
Location: Cochrane Street to Conduit Road, Central-Mid-Levels, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The world's longest covered outdoor escalator system, threading past Soho, Hollywood Road and tower blocks; the Queen's Road to Hollywood Road stretch is the photographic core. Why: Layers of tong lau, shops and commuters from above; near the Graham Street mural and Man Mo Temple. Free.

Name: sky100 Observation Deck (ICC)
Location: 100/F, International Commerce Centre, 1 Austin Road West, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Indoor observation deck on the 100th floor of ICC with 360-degree harbour views. Why: Highest public viewing deck, but it closed for renovation from 17 May 2025 with a reopening target of H1 2026 that I could not confirm. Free alternatives: TST promenade and West Kowloon waterfront.
